\newcommand{\resultstext}{Across all 707 training frames (1,154 annotator records, 8,199 annotated filaments), the 5-fold out-of-fold pipeline achieves $\mathrm{PQ}=0.458$ (95\% date-bootstrap CI 0.449--0.466), $\mathrm{SQ}=0.691$ and $\mathrm{RQ}=0.663$ (5,263 true positives, 2,414 false positives and 2,936 false negatives, emitting 6.66 instances per frame on validation and 6.78 on the 180 test frames). Fold-wise PQ is stable across the five date-grouped splits (0.462, 0.464, 0.442, 0.468 and 0.460; Fig.~\ref{fig:eval}, middle). Among overlapping prediction--annotation pairs, the mean IoU is 0.607 and the mean Dice is 0.736, compared with 0.517 and 0.660 between human annotators on the 296 multi-record frames (Fig.~\ref{fig:eval}, left). Out of 8,199 ground-truth filaments, 78.6\% (6,441) overlap exactly one prediction (one-to-one), 19.4\% (1,593) are missed, and only 2.0\% (165) touch two or more predictions; conversely, 82.5\% (6,336) of predictions overlap a single annotation, 14.6\% (1,124) are unannotated false alarms, and 2.8\% (216) bridge two or more annotations (Fig.~\ref{fig:eval}, right).}
\newcommand{\examplescaption}{The pipeline captures thin filaments and narrow barbs across GONG sites (e.g.\ 2015-04-21~Bh, 2012-05-19~Th, 2014-02-05~Bh, 2015-07-06~Th); typical disagreements occur on faint active-region fibrils or fragmented remnants where annotators also differ (2015-01-13~Ch, 2014-11-12~Bh).}
\newcommand{\discussiontext}{\emph{Strengths.} Decoupling detection at 1280~px from segmentation on $512\times512$ native-resolution crops preserves 2--5~px filament barbs ($\mathrm{SQ}=0.691$ vs.\ $0.633$ between humans) while keeping one-to-many fragmentation below 3\%. Training the detector on every annotator record turns box confidence into a calibrated estimate of annotator consensus, which raises PQ by $+0.018$ over an untuned confidence floor ($c{=}0.10$) and $+0.040$ over a strict floor ($c{=}0.40$). Flip TTA with Weighted Boxes Fusion contributes $+0.005$ PQ mainly through recognition quality ($\mathrm{RQ}: 0.657\to0.663$). \emph{Weaknesses and future work.} Because the segmenter is restricted to a padded detector box, long curved filaments whose box is truncated by the detector cannot grow outside the crop; naive inference-time crop padding ($p{=}0.35$) lowers PQ to $0.444$ due to scale mismatch with training ($p{=}0.20$). Training the crop segmenter with random box truncation and multi-scale padding, or adding a lightweight graph-stitching head for broken filament chains, is the most direct path to further gains.}
